title: Daily Briefing
intro: A briefing bot runs on a schedule, gathers from a fixed set of sources, and puts one thing in front of you at a set time. It is the most reliable category on this site because the job is narrow and the failure mode is obvious — if the briefing is wrong or late you notice immediately, which is not true of most agent work. The listings differ mainly in what they read: some pull only your own calendar and inbox, others sweep news, X, repositories and dashboards. More sources is not better. The briefings people keep are the ones that leave things out, and a bot that summarises fourteen feeds every morning gets skimmed and then ignored within a fortnight. Look for one where you can set what counts as worth reporting, and check whether it stays quiet on a slow day — the good ones do.

bots.fitReason: A weekday morning news scout in your own timezone, run on a schedule or triggered with a word — the plain version of this job with nothing bolted on. You define the beat, which also means a vague beat gets you a vague briefing.
Samples your X feed through the day and delivers one clustered 7am brief, read-only and no posting. Single-source by design: if your morning read is more than X, this is not the whole briefing.

Morning transcript recap of channels you nominate, and it stays quiet when nothing new has landed — the discipline this category lives or dies on. Fixed to YouTube via TranscriptAPI, so it is one feed, not a sweep.

Learns your beat from your recent posts, then sends a weekday end-of-day brief of what you'd actually want flagged from X. Evening rather than morning, and the beat inference is only as good as your own posting history.

Weekday morning briefing that pairs overnight tech news with the email that actually needs action, delivered before work. Aimed squarely at tech writers and editors; a different beat will need reconfiguring.
A fixed roster of official model-lab release channels, read at 07:30 EAT and summarised once. Narrow by construction — useful only if AI model releases are the thing you need to know about daily.
Morning digest of the day ahead plus a next-day briefing at night, with addresses and times attached. It is a calendar briefing and nothing more, so no news, mail or dashboards.

Scans a fixed list of 21 Grok Bot accounts twice each weekday and delivers only posts that clear its bar, otherwise it says nothing — exactly the restraint this job wants. Chinese-language output and a very narrow beat.
